deep.reconstruction:
Context, partly my reading: this page belongs to Riemann's genus-3 theory (p=3). The curve is the plane quartic sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta)=0. Here x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta are linear forms in three homogeneous coordinates. They are tied by the normalized relations L0 = x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta = 0, L1 = a*x+b*y+c*z+xi/a+eta/b+zeta/c = 0 and L2 = a'x+b'y+c'z+xi/a'+eta/b'+zeta/c' = 0. (Riemann writes alpha, beta, gamma; I use a, b, c in places.) The following page shows these relations explicitly. A fourth relation of the same shape, with alpha'', beta'', gamma'', follows from the three via 1+lam*alpha+lam'*alpha' = lam''*alpha'' and 1+lam/alpha+lam'/alpha' = lam''/alpha'' (and likewise for beta, gamma), as on the next page. The page studies when the curve degenerates. A plane quartic has 28 bitangents ('Geraden'). For each of the 63 nonzero half-periods ('63 Perioden', characteristics written as 3-over-3 bit columns), there is a 'Gruppe' of six pairs of bitangents (a Steiner complex). Riemann asks for the quantities whose vanishing makes the two lines of every pair of a group coincide. I read this as the curve acquiring a node whose vanishing cycle has that half-period class. Such a node merges 12 bitangents into 6 double tangents through the node; 16 genuine bitangents remain.

(1) First-type conditions. Write (alpha beta gamma) for det[[1,1,1],[alpha,beta,gamma],[alpha',beta',gamma']]. This determinant is attached to one characteristic. The variants with some entries inverted (alpha -> 1/alpha etc., i.e. swapping x<->xi and so on) are attached to other characteristics. A further determinant is attached to 011/111; its rows are [1,1,1] and [beta*gamma/(1-beta*gamma), alpha*gamma/(1-alpha*gamma), alpha*beta/(1-alpha*beta)] in unprimed and primed form. Alongside it Riemann notes alpha''=beta''=gamma''=1.

Why (alpha beta gamma)=0 gives a node (my verification): some combination of L0, L1, L2 then kills x, y, z. This gives a linear relation among xi, eta, zeta alone, so these three lines are concurrent. The rationalized quartic (x*xi+y*eta-z*zeta)^2-4*x*xi*y*eta is homogeneous of degree 2 in (xi,eta,zeta). Hence it has a double point where xi=eta=zeta=0.

(2) Main statement: the coincidence of the lines in all pairs of a group is equivalent to a certain relation holding between three lines of different pairs of the group. The sentence is incomplete in the manuscript.

(3) Classification of the 63 cases by how they look in these coordinates:
- I: (alpha beta gamma)=0, with alpha''=beta''=gamma''=0; 32 cases. My count: 4 choices of three relations out of L0..L3, times 8 inversion patterns.
- II: alpha=beta, with alpha'beta''=alpha''beta'; 18 cases. My count: 3 variable pairs times 6 pairs of relations.
- III: (A-B)/(A'-B') = (A-G)/(A'-G'), where A=alpha+1/alpha, B=beta+1/beta, G=gamma+1/gamma, primes analogous; 6 cases. Riemann also writes the three ratios (A-B)/(A-G), (A'-B')/(A'-G') and (C-D)/(C-E), with C=alpha/alpha'+alpha'/alpha, D=beta/beta'+beta'/beta, E=gamma/gamma'+gamma'/gamma. My interpretation: subtracting the defining equations of the fourth relation gives two conics in (lam,lam') through the origin: lam(A-B)+lam'(A'-B')+lam*lam'(C-D)=0 and its gamma-analogue. Condition III says their linear parts are proportional, so the origin becomes a tangential (double) intersection.
- IV: alpha=beta and alpha'=beta', giving alpha''=beta''; 6 cases.
- V: alpha=alpha'=beta=beta'=gamma=gamma'=1; 1 case.
Total 32+18+6+6+1 = 63. Riemann remarks that exchanging the vanishing half-group with the other half maps III to IV and maps I, II, V to themselves.

(4) Local analysis of case V. Put alpha=1+a*lam, beta=1+b*lam, gamma=1+c*lam. Then L1-L0 = a*lam*(x-xi)+b*lam*(y-eta)+c*lam*(z-zeta) + a^2*lam^2*xi+b^2*lam^2*eta+c^2*lam^2*zeta + O(lam^3), using 1/(1+a*lam)-1 = -a*lam+a^2*lam^2-... In the limit x=xi, y=eta, z=zeta, and L0 gives x+y+z=0. With (x-xi)/lam etc. finite, dividing by lam^2 gives a*(x-xi)/lam+b*(y-eta)/lam+c*(z-zeta)/lam + a^2*xi+b^2*eta+c^2*zeta = 0, and the same with a', b', c'.

(5) Local analysis of case IV. Riemann writes L0/lam. He writes L1 as alpha*(x+y)+(xi+eta)/alpha+gamma*z+zeta/gamma+(beta-alpha)*y+(alpha-beta)*eta/alpha^2, divided by lam. This uses eta/beta ~ eta/alpha-(beta-alpha)*eta/alpha^2 to first order in beta-alpha; L2 is treated likewise. The page ends with (1/lam)(alpha beta gamma), presumably the rescaled determinant in this limit.
errors: Case IV: the term (alpha-beta)*eta/(lam*alpha^2) is only the first-order expansion of eta/beta - eta/alpha. This is legitimate as a leading-order computation but not exact.
Case V: the expansion of 1/(1+a*lam) is truncated at order lam^2. This is correct to the order used.
The first III condition was rewritten as a list of three ratios. The struck-out version (alpha-1/alpha)/(alpha'-1/alpha') = ... was rejected by Riemann himself.
The sentence stating the necessary and sufficient condition is grammatically incomplete: the relation that is supposed to 'take place' (stattfinden) is never named.
Case II: the struck line in Case II reads '18 ähnliche Fälle', the same count that is then written again, so the deletion appears to be a rewrite of the line rather than a correction of the number.

results.what: Normal form of the genus-3 curve: sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0, with six linear forms tied by three symmetric linear relations (alpha, beta, gamma; alpha', beta', gamma') and an induced fourth relation (alpha'', beta'', gamma'').
results.modern_name: Riemann's representation of a plane quartic via a Steiner complex / three pairs of bitangents
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous, Werke 1876, 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3'); Weber 1876

results.what: The 63 nonzero half-periods correspond to the 63 groups of six bitangent pairs. Degenerations in which all six pairs of a group coalesce are classified into 63 conditions on the moduli, of types I-V (32+18+6+6+1).
results.modern_name: Nodal degeneration of plane quartics: the discriminant splits into 63 components over the level-2 moduli space; the 12 bitangents of a Steiner complex become 6 double tangents through the node
results.usually_credited_to: Classical: Zeuthen (1873) and Salmon for the coalescing of bitangents at a node; level-2 structure of the discriminant in later 19th/20th-century literature

results.what: A vanishing determinant (alpha beta gamma) makes xi, eta, zeta concurrent, giving a node of the quartic.
results.modern_name: Singular point where three of the bitangent forms vanish simultaneously

results.what: Local expansions near the degenerate parameter values (cases IV and V) to obtain the limiting linear relations.
results.modern_name: First-order degeneration analysis / blow-up of the parameter point

deep.surprise_reason: The framework (sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0 with alpha, beta, gamma moduli) is Riemann's own, published posthumously. New here is an explicit unpublished classification of the 63 nodal degenerations by half-period, with the counts 32+18+6+6+1 and local expansions. This is a notable unpublished detail anticipating classical work on degenerations of quartics, but not a major theorem credited to someone else.

checkable.asserts: Expansion used in case V: xi/alpha - xi = -a*lam*xi + a^2*lam^2*xi + O(lam^3); equals 0.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,X,Y,Z=symbols('x y z X Y Z'); t=symbols('t'); F=(x*X+y*Y-z*Z)**2-4*x*X*y*Y; expand(F.subs({X:t*X,Y:t*Y,Z:t*Z})-t**2*F)
checkable.asserts: The rationalized quartic is homogeneous of degree 2 in (xi,eta,zeta) (written X,Y,Z), so it has a double point where these vanish (case I); result is 0.
Case IV first-order term: eta/beta - eta/alpha ~ (alpha-beta)*eta/alpha^2 with beta=alpha+d; equals 0.
Identity underlying the III-type ratios: lam''^2 = 1+lam^2+lam'^2+lam*A+lam'*A'+lam*lam'*C; equals 0.
The five types exhaust the 63 nonzero half-periods.

transcription_corrections: In the second III line the numerator 'alpha^2+1/alpha' should read alpha+1/alpha, matching the structure (A-B)/(A-G).

The determinant labels '(alpha/beta beta gamma)', '(alpha/beta 1/gamma)', '(alpha beta/gamma gamma)' are probably inversion patterns like (1/alpha beta gamma), (alpha 1/beta 1/gamma) etc. The 8 patterns of inverting alpha, beta, gamma fit the 3-bit characteristic labels.
'16 gemeinschaftlichen Ebenen' is uncertain; the context (bitangents) suggests the sixteen remaining lines or tangents. The reading is doubtful.
In III the condition 'alpha''=alpha' is uncertain; it may be alpha''=1 or alpha''=alpha'.
The deleted 'Reihe' was replaced by 'Gruppe' throughout, as already marked.
